question.:question/problem: Find the particular solution to the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={e}^{4(x + 4)-y}$ that satisfies $y(-4)=5.$

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={e}^{4(x + 4)-y} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={e}^{4(x + 4)}\cdot {e}^{-y} \\ {e}^{y}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={e}^{4(x + 4)} \\ \int {e}^{y}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int {e}^{4(x + 4)}\,\text{d}x \\ \int {e}^{y}\,\text{d}y & =\int {e}^{4(x + 4)}\,\text{d}x \\ {e}^{y} & =\frac{{e}^{4(x + 4)}}{4}+C\,.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{y}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{{e}^{4(x + 4)}}{4}+C) \\ y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{{e}^{4(x + 4)}}{4}+C)\end{aligned}

$$
y=\operatorname{ln}⁡\left(\frac{{e}^{4(x + 4)}+4{e}^{5}-1}{4}\right).

$$
